slides.title: One word for your company’s strategy?
slides.headline: One word for your company’s strategy?
notes: Preserve the template’s one-word strategy exercise. Ask what differences reveal about the team’s shared picture. Transition into a clearer three-year destination, not a full competitive-analysis workshop.

artwork.alt: Three leaders write independently before comparing their answers.

slides.title: Strategy creates a unique and valuable position.
slides.headline: Strategy creates a unique and valuable position.
notes: Ask how the company creates value differently. A financial target alone does not describe a strategy.
Connect to the source’s confidently differentiated teaching.
slides.support: A different set of activities makes that position possible.
body: Michael Porter’s definition, as taught by Shannon.

slides.title: Compete to be unique.
slides.headline: Compete to be unique.
notes: Ask what would make the customer choose this company for a different reason.
Do not start the later-quarter market and differentiation workshops here.
Choosing a valuable position means choosing what not to do. Different activities must reinforce one another.
Better operations alone do not establish a differentiated position. Later workshops test customers, competition and activity fit.

panels.heading: Best on the same dimensions
panels.support: Try to outperform rivals at the same activities.

panels.heading: Unique value
panels.support: Choose a valuable position supported by different activities.

slides.title: Build a strategy you can test and refine.
slides.headline: Build a strategy you can test and refine.
notes: Shannon connects external and internal analysis to strategy and execution.
The kickoff sets a starting direction. Later quarters validate customers, market position and differentiating activities.
Internal analysis examines the company and how its work flows. External analysis examines customers, competitors and the market.
Kickoff capabilities are a starting hypothesis. Market Map, Core Customer, Attribution and Activity Fit workshops validate it later.

panels.heading: Understand
panels.support: Study the market and the business.

panels.heading: Choose
panels.support: Define position, scope and connected activities.

panels.heading: Learn
panels.support: Execute, observe results and test assumptions.
